sections.heading: Superlatives and el único que
sections.body:
After a superlative or *el único / el primero / el último que*, both moods are possible:

- **Indicative** — you state a fact about a known set: *Es la mejor película que he visto.* (It's the best film I've seen — I've seen them.) *Es el único que me entiende.*
- **Subjunctive** — you generalise or leave the set open, often more emphatic or subjective: *Es la mejor película que haya visto nunca.* (…that I've ever seen.) *Eres la única persona que me entienda de verdad.*

With *nunca / jamás* the subjunctive is especially common: *Es lo más bonito que me hayan dicho jamás.*

sections.heading: Free relatives: indicative or subjunctive
sections.body:
Relatives without an antecedent follow the known / unknown rule:

*Haz lo que quieras.* (whatever you want — not known) vs. *Haz lo que quieres.* (do what you want — I know what it is)
*Los que lleguen tarde no podrán entrar.* (whoever arrives late — future, unknown) vs. *Los que llegaron tarde no pudieron entrar.*
*Donde tú digas.* (Wherever you say.) vs. *Nos vemos donde dijiste.*

sections.heading: Other tricky contexts
sections.body:
- *el que* + subjunctive as a subject clause (the fact that): *El que no hayas llamado me molestó.* (The fact that you didn't call bothered me.)
- *de ahí que, no porque, sin que, antes de que* → always subjunctive
- *es que* / *lo que pasa es que* → indicative (explanation)
- *quizás / tal vez* → either mood; *a lo mejor* → indicative
- *ojalá* → subjunctive (present = possible, imperfect = unlikely, pluperfect = past regret)
- *decir que* → indicative (report) or subjunctive (order) — see C1.1
- *Que* + subjunctive alone = wish or command: *Que tengas suerte.* *¡Que pase el siguiente!* (Next, please!)

He was the first to arrive.
Haz lo que quieras.
Do whatever you want.

Los que lleguen tarde no podrán entrar.
Whoever arrives late won't be able to get in.

The fact that you didn't call bothered me.

Good luck.
